To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gene expression arrays can be generated from sub-nanogram quantities of total RNA and that all three amplification techniques tested were accurate.
gene expression arrays can be generated with sub-nanograms of input RNA.
gene expression profiling is feasible and accurate with sub-nanograms of total RNA using linear or logarithmic amplification methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method of RNA amplification for gene expression profiling of very low-input RNA samples.
the accuracy of RNA amplification and gene expression analysis at sub-nanograms of input RNA.
the development of a new technique of amplification of RNA from a small number of cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amplification methods are equally accurate, but the data analysis methods are critical for the accurate analysis of the amplified data.
the accuracy of gene-expression profiling from sub-nanogram quantities of RNA is dependent on the amplification method, the data processing and the genes of interest.
RNA amplification methods work well for low input amounts of RNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amplification methods tested were all accurate for low-input quantities of total RNA, but the accuracy was best for high intensity genes.
all three methods can be used to generate reliable data from low input quantities, however, we recommend that the Arcturus RibaAmp HS method be used when working with sub-nanograms of total RNA.
all 3 amplifications methods can be used for low-input RNA expression analysis, but the T7 and RiboAmp amplification methods are more accurate for high intensity genes than the balanced PCR method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of amplification method is less important than the quality of the data generated from each method.
it is possible to generate accurate gene expression profiles from small numbers of cells.
it is possible to get good quality data from small amounts of RNA.
